item.title: Sixth Circuit Rules Out Retaliation Claims Under Rehab Act Section 504: What Smith Means for Federally Funded Programs
item.description: Takeaways In Smith v. Mich. Dep’t of Corr., the Sixth Circuit held that Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act does not provide a private cause of action for retaliation, addressing the unsettled statutory basis for this type of claim. The Sixth Circuit rejected decades of multiple courts’ long-accepted assumptions that such claims exist under Section 504. item.title: Minor Questions to Belabor in the NIL Era: The Status of High School Athletes
item.description: For years, many have advocated that participation in college athletics is “work” and, consequently, college athletes should be treated as “employees” of the schools they attend under federal and state labor and employment laws. item.title: Updates for Overtime and Tip Reporting Obligations for 2025
item.description: As we wrote on July 14, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBA) contains a provision providing a tax deduction for employees’ overtime income in 2025 through 2028. Originally, the data regarding such overtime income was to be reported on a W-2 form. item.title: Relationship Limits: 11th Circuit Reins in Scope of “Relating To” in Insurance Policy Exclusions
item.description: Insurers often rely on introductory phrases in exclusions, such as the phrase “relating to,” to expand the scope of exclusions beyond all reasonable bounds. The Eleventh Circuit recently reaffirmed that insurance exclusions — including those broadly drafted to exclude any claim “relating to” an excluded risk — should have meaningful limits and must be interpreted narrowly. item.title: Preparing for the UK Employment Rights Bill
